subject: Request for SLA apportionment after multi-path latency — ACME Tech
messages:
From: James Li <james.li@acmetech.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: High tail latency on 2026-06-29 — where does this land against our SLA?

Hi Lauren,

We observed sustained 95th/99th percentile tail latency spikes for our API calls between 03:10–03:52 UTC on 2026-06-29. Our monitoring shows a mix of error responses and timeouts for about 4% of requests during that window, and degraded responses (increased latencies but not errors) for another ~9%.

ACME's SRE flagged that the redwood edge region for our traffic had an operator maintenance window at the same time, but we also saw DNS failover activity from our provider which may have routed requests across a downstream CDN partner chain. Our procurement team has asked whether this should be treated as an exclusion (provider maintenance) or whether the partial degradation portion is attributable to Redwood. We need clarity and an estimate of any SLA credit.

Attachments: sample request ids, probe traces (zipped).

Please advise next steps and whether you need anything else to triage.

Thanks,
James
Senior SRE, ACME Tech
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: James Li <james.li@acmetech.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-29T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: High tail latency on 2026-06-29 — where does this land against our SLA?

James — thanks for the quick heads up and the traces. We're pulling together a consolidated timeline. Initial read: there was a scheduled maintenance on our regional edge routers (announce at 2026-06-28 22:00 UTC) that started an automated light-weight rebalancing at 03:05 UTC; that work completed at 03:40 UTC.

However, our telemetry also shows a DNS flapping event reported by one of ACME's upstream CDNs at 03:07–03:20 UTC that caused an out-of-band fanout to an alternate CDN path. During that overlap we see amplified tail latency on requests that hit the alternate path.

Working plan: Marissa and Engineering will quantify minutes of full outage-equivalent (errors/timeouts) and minutes of partial degradation (latency above SLO but still serving). Then we'll propose an apportionment approach consistent with our SLA (we usually exclude maintenance windows but split responsibility for partial degradations when third-party failover is involved).

I'll follow up with the timeline and a suggested credit split.

—Ben
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-30T10:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: High tail latency on 2026-06-29 — timeline and proposed apportionment

Team — digging into traces (see attached). Key points: 
- Our maintenance window was narrow and intended as configuration rollforward for route optimization; control-plane logs show active maintenance from 03:05–03:40 UTC (35 minutes). We flag that as a declared maintenance window per section 5.1 of the contract.
- Within that interval: 
  * 03:07–03:20 UTC — DNS flapping at ACME upstream (external) which produced ~65% of observed error/timeouts in the sample set.
  * 03:20–03:40 UTC — increased tail latency on ~11% of requests even after DNS stabilized; looking at RTTs and our edge metrics, roughly half of that appears correlated to our route rebalancer pulling sessions across a path with suboptimal peering.
- Outside 03:05–03:40 window we do not see sustained SLA breaches.

Recommended apportionment for discussion with ACME: 
- Full outage-equivalent minutes (errors/timeouts) during 03:07–03:20 UTC: attribute 65% to ACME upstream CDN (third party) and 35% to Redwood (because our rebalancer increased session churn during maintenance and amplified failure rate).
- Partial degradation minutes (03:20–03:40 UTC): suggest a 60/40 split in Redwood's favor (60% ACME / 40% Redwood) given DNS instability was the trigger and our rebalancer contributed to prolonged recovery time.

Proposed remedy: offer a one-time credit equal to 0.75x daily pro-rata SLA credit (split according to apportionment above) plus a technical action plan: (1) disable aggressive session rebalancing during declared maintenance windows for this customer, and (2) add a probe-based pre-check that defers maintenance if upstream DNS is unstable.

I'll attach the SLO calc spreadsheet with minute-level buckets. Ben, can you take this to ACME and see if Procurement will accept the split? If they push back, escalate to Lauren for an executive decision.

—Marissa
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, James Li <james.li@acmetech.com>, Procurement <procurement@acmetech.com>
Date: 2026-07-01T17:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: High tail latency on 2026-06-29 — request for SLA apportionment after multi-path latency — ACME Tech

Hi James / ACME team — thanks for the patience while we completed the analysis. I want to be explicit and pragmatic.

Summary: 
- There was a declared Redwood maintenance window (03:05–03:40 UTC). Per contract, declared maintenance is normally excluded from SLA credits. That said, where maintenance materially increases the severity/duration of client-facing impact because of interaction with a third party, we make exceptions.
- After reviewing Marissa's timeline and the sample traces, Redwood accepts responsibility for a portion of the impact caused by our rebalancer behavior during the maintenance. We propose the apportionment Marissa outlined: 65/35 split for outage-equivalent minutes and 60/40 split for partial degradation minutes (ACME/Redwood).

Remedy: Redwood will issue a credit calculated as follows and applied to ACME's next billing cycle: 
1) Compute total customer-impact minutes (errors + partial degrade buckets) from 03:07–03:40.
2) Apply the apportionment percentages to isolate Redwood's responsibility.
3) Redwood credit = pro-rata portion of daily service fee * responsibility fraction * 0.75 (goodwill multiplier).

Additionally, we will: 
- Implement the two technical mitigations Marissa recommended within 30 days and provide ACME a short runbook for maintenance coordination.
- Provide a post-mortem summary and a short ISO-style timeline in HubSpot (link above).

If Procurement accepts, Ben can confirm the credit amount and we'll issue a formal credit memo. If ACME prefers an alternative (larger credit or different split), let's get that proposal in writing and we can take to Exec for review.

James — apologies for the customer impact and thank you for working through the details with us. Ben — please follow up with a short note to Procurement and include the spreadsheet.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
VP, Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
